rows.acip: CHU 'BAB KLUNG LA YI DVAGS RNAG BLO YANG , , ZHES SOGS KYI SKABS SU MTHA' DPYAD PA LA, CHU KLUNG RNAG KHRAG TU SNANG BA'I YI DVAGS KYI MIG SHES DANG , BSE RU'I NANG DU SKRA SHAD 'DZAG PAR SNANG BA'I RAB RIB CAN GYI MIG SHES DANG , SA GZHI KENG RUS KYIS KHYAB PAR SNANG BA'I KENG RUS GSAL SNANG CAN GYI TING NGE 'DZIN DANG BCAS PA RNAMS KYI YUL DE DANG , DER YOD MED RNAM PA KUN DU MTSUNGS SAM MI MTSUNGS ZHE NA,
rows.wylie: chu 'bab klung la yi dvags rnag blo yang , , zhes sogs kyi skabs su mtha' dpyad pa la, chu klung rnag khrag tu snang ba'i yi dvags kyi mig shes dang , bse ru'i nang du skra shad 'dzag par snang ba'i rab rib can gyi mig shes dang , sa gzhi keng rus kyis khyab par snang ba'i keng rus gsal snang can gyi ting nge 'dzin dang bcas pa rnams kyi yul de dang , der yod med rnam pa kun du mtshungs sam mi mtshungs zhe na
rows.english: Here we will analyze the statement [from Entering the Middle Way, by Master Chandrakirti (650 AD)] where it says, "...The mind of a craving spirit as well, which sees a stream of water as pus." One may begin with the following question: Let's consider the objects of the following states of mind: the visual consciousness of a craving spirit where a river of water looks like pus and blood; the visual consciousness of a person with a kind of cataract where a clean white porcelain basin looks like a hair has fallen into it; and that kind of meditation where you visualize skeletons--where you imagine that the entire surface of the earth is covered with the bones of corpses. Are all these objects completely equivalent, as far as being something that exists or doesn't exist?

rows.acip: KHA CIG NA RE, RGYU MTSAN DE NYID KYI PHYIR NA, CHOS THAMS CAD LA 'DI YIN 'DI MIN GANG DU YANG BZUNG DU MED DO, , ZHES ZER NA, SANGS RGYAS PA'I GRUB MTHA' DANG , PHYI ROL PA'I GRUB MTHA' LA BZANG NGAN DANG , BDAG CAG GI STON PA DANG , PHYI ROL PA'I STON PA LA MCHOG DMAN SOGS MED PAR THAL,
rows.wylie: kha cig na re, rgyu mtshan de nyid kyi phyir na, chos thams cad la 'di yin 'di min gang du yang bzung du med do, , zhes zer na, sangs rgyas pa'i grub mtha' dang , phyi rol pa'i grub mtha' la bzang ngan dang , bdag cag gi ston pa dang , phyi rol pa'i ston pa la mchog dman sogs med par thal
rows.english: Someone may make the following claim: Given the statements that have come above, the fact is that we should never again consider anything as being one way or the other. Well then, you must be suggesting that the system of the Buddha is all the same as the system of every non-Buddhist belief, that there is no difference in their correctness at all. And you must be saying too that we could never state that our Teacher was the highest teacher, and that the teachers of the non- Buddhists are lesser.

rows.acip: CHOS THAMS CAD LA 'DI YIN 'DI MIN GANG DU YANG BZUNG DU MED PA'I PHYIR, 'DOD NA, YOD PAR THAL, BDAG NI STON PA GZHAN SPANGS NAS, , KHYOD LA SKYABS SU MCHI LAGS KYI, , CI SLAD CE NA KHYED NYID NI, , SKYON MI MNGA' ZHING YON TAN RDZOGS, , ZHES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: chos thams cad la 'di yin 'di min gang du yang bzung du med pa'i phyir, 'dod na, yod par thal, bdag ni ston pa gzhan spangs nas, , khyod la skyabs su mchi lags kyi, , ci slad ce na khyed nyid ni, , skyon mi mnga' zhing yon tan rdzogs, , zhes gsungs pa'i phyir
rows.english: And you must be suggesting all this, for you have claimed that we should never again consider anything as being one way or the other. Now if you should agree that none of the differences mentioned above exist, we must reply that they do, for as the verse says: All other teachers now I've given up, And go for refuge now to only You; Why? Because it's You alone who has No fault, and perfected every good.

rows.english: "You have mentioned," one may begin, "sustenance consisting of contact, and so on. Just what is the nature of each of these types of sustenance?" Contact, mental movement, and consciousness that come with stain are each a kind of sustenance. In their unstained form they can't be called sustenance, for sustenance is defined by its function of perpetuating this suffering life, whereas the stainless act to bring it to a stop. As sutra says, It functions to keep alive those beings who have already come out, and to nourish them; it functions to provide aid to those still in the state of seeking their next life.

rows.english: The one-day vows are called "staying close" because they help you stay close to nirvana in the sense of taking you there. The lifetime vows for laymen and laywomen are called "close to virtue" because they help you be close to virtue, which here refers to nirvana. The vows of male novices and female novices are called "way to virtue" because those who possess these vows have entered the way, that is the path, which leads to virtue, again referring to nirvana. The vows of an intermediate nun are called "versed in virtue" because these women are versing themselves in the twelve rules, in order to be able to keep the vows of a fully ordained nun. Fully ordained monks and fully ordained nuns are called "begging for virtue" because they are begging, that is seeking, that state of virtue: nirvana. rows.acip: [III.157-8a] REG PA'I ZAS LA SOGS PA DE DAG GI NGO BO GANG ZHE NA, REG PA DANG SEMS PA DANG RNAM PAR SHES PA NI ZAG PA DANG BCAS PA ZAS YIN GYI, ZAG MED ZAS MIN TE, ZAS KYI DON NI SRID PA GSO BAR BYED PA YIN NA, ZAG MED NI SRID PA ZAD BYED YIN PA'I PHYIR DANG , MDO LAS, SEMS CAN BYUNG BA RNAMS GNAS PAR BYED PA DANG , 'TSO BAR BYED PA DANG , SRID PA TSOL BA RNAMS LA PHAN 'DOGS PAR BYED PA'O, , ZHES DANG ,
rows.wylie: [iii.157-8a] reg pa'i zas la sogs pa de dag gi ngo bo gang zhe na, reg pa dang sems pa dang rnam par shes pa ni zag pa dang bcas pa zas yin gyi, zag med zas min te, zas kyi don ni srid pa gso bar byed pa yin na, zag med ni srid pa zad byed yin pa'i phyir dang , mdo las, sems can byung ba rnams gnas par byed pa dang , 'tsho bar byed pa dang , srid pa tshol ba rnams la phan 'dogs par byed pa'o, , zhes dang
rows.english: "You have mentioned," one may begin, "sustenance consisting of contact, and so on. Just what is the nature of each of these types of sustenance?" Contact, mental movement, and consciousness that come with stain are each a kind of sustenance. In their unstained form they can't be called sustenance, for sustenance is defined by its function of perpetuating this suffering life, whereas the stainless act to bring it to a stop. As sutra says, It functions to keep alive those beings who have already come out, and to nourish them; it functions to provide aid to those still in the state of seeking their next life.

rows.english: There is no other, separate place for the formless realm. A person who is born there must first have attained single-pointed concentration relating to the formless realm, and must not have lost this ability since that time. When such a person dies and migrates, he is born into the formless realm at the very place where he died, the four "name" heaps of the formless realm coming into existence there. There are however four kinds of levels to the formless realm, depending on the relative quality of that meditation to which one had given rise and which had caused his birth there. These are the levels known as the "Door of Limitless Space" and so on.

rows.english: In response Subhuti replies, O Conqueror, it would not be so. And suppose you were to ask why—for what reason—it is so. It is because the One Gone Thus has said that other people's seeing something as a self and the rest, as described by the One Gone Thus, are ways of seeing things that would never exist anyway, at least in an ultimate sense, since the views themselves fail, and the objects which they believe they see prove to be non-existent. And this is precisely why we can call them "seeing something as a self" and the rest. Understanding & seeing

rows.acip: ZAB MO NI YUL GYI KHYAD PAR TE STONG PA NYID YIN LA, SNANG BA ZHES BYA BA'I TING NGE 'DZIN NI YUL CAN GYI KHYAD PAR TE, DE LTA BU'I ZAB MO RTOGS PA'I TING NGE 'DZIN DE LA SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA STE MNYAM PAR BZHAG PA'O,,
rows.wylie: zab mo ni yul gyi khyad par te stong pa nyid yin la, snang ba zhes bya ba'i ting nge 'dzin ni yul can gyi khyad par te, de lta bu'i zab mo rtogs pa'i ting nge 'dzin de la snyoms par zhugs pa ste mnyam par bzhag pa'o
rows.english: The word “profound” conveys the detail of the object—meaning emptiness itself. And then “awareness” specifies the subject state of mind involved: the deep meditation with this name. Lord Buddha then “went into” this deep meditation, meaning that he set his mind into this kind of meditative balance.

rows.acip: RANG YAB YUM SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS SPYI BO NAS MGRIN PAR SLEB PA NA DGA' BA, MGRIN PA NAS SNYING GAR SLEB PA NA MCHOG DGA', SNYING GNAS LTE BAR SLEB PA NA KHYAD DGA', LTE BA NAS GSANG GNAS KYI RTZER SLEB PA NA LHAN CIG SKYES BA'I DGA' BA SKYES, BDE STONG DBYER MED KYI LHAN SKYES KYI DGA' BA NI DBANG GSUM BA'I NGO BO YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: rang yab yum snyoms par zhugs pa'i byang chub kyi sems spyi bo nas mgrin par sleb pa na dga' ba, mgrin pa nas snying gar sleb pa na mchog dga', snying gnas lte bar sleb pa na khyad dga', lte ba nas gsang gnas kyi rtser sleb pa na lhan cig skyes ba'i dga' ba skyes, bde stong dbyer med kyi lhan skyes kyi dga' ba ni dbang gsum ba'i ngo bo yin no
rows.english: (Speak then to the disciple these words, so they understand what is happening:) The two of you, The Man and Woman, Go into union. The Wish for enlightenment Flows from the top of your heads To your throats, Bringing you ecstasy. From your throats then It flows to your hearts, Bringing you high ecstasy. Flowing from your hearts To your navels, It brings you incredible ecstasy. From your navels it flows To the tips of your secret places, Bringing you simultaneous bliss. And it is this simultaneous bliss, Indivisible ecstasy and voidness, Which is the true essence Of this, the third initiation.

rows.acip: (ZHES KHONG DU CHUD PAR BYA ZHING, DE'I TSE SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LA BRTEN NAS BDE STONG GI YE SHES DNGOS SU SKYES PA DANG, DE SKYES PAR MOS BA DANG BDE BA CHEN PO SKYES BA'AM SKYES PAR MOS BA SOGS KYI DBANG PO'I RIM PAS SHER DBANG THOB LUGS SNA TSOGS ZHIG 'ONG BA NGO 'PHROD NGES BYA LA, DE NAS MIG DAR DKROL LO,,)

rows.english: (At this point, one either experiences, directly, the wisdom of bliss and voidness which comes through the practice of union--or else one only imagines they have experienced it.  One experiences great bliss, or else only imagines that they have.  Be sure to acquaint the disciple with these and the other possibilities that occur during the empowerment; let them know that there are different ways in which one may be granted this Initiation of Infinite Wisdom. And then take off their blindfold.) 100) The purity which is granted

rows.acip: ZHABS GA-YAS BSKUMS SHING GA-YON BRKYANGS PA'I STABS KYIS BZHUGS PA, YAB YUM SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA'I THUGS KA'I H'Um GI 'OD ZER GYIS BKUG PA'I KHRO BO BCU ZHAL DU BCUG NAS ZHU BA RDO RJE'I LAM NAS YUM GYI PADMAR ZHUGS PA'I THIG LE BCU LAS H'Um RING PO BCU DANG DE LAS KHRO BO BCUR GYUR,
rows.wylie: zhabs ga-yas bskums shing ga-yon brkyangs pa'i stabs kyis bzhugs pa, yab yum snyoms par zhugs pa'i thugs ka'i hUM gi 'od zer gyis bkug pa'i khro bo bcu zhal du bcug nas zhu ba rdo rje'i lam nas yum gyi padmar zhugs pa'i thig le bcu las hUM ring po bcu dang de las khro bo bcur gyur
rows.english: I am standing with my right leg bent And my left leg extended. As Husband and Wife we join together in meditation, And from the hung at our precious heart Come rays of light Which bring down the ten Wrathful Ones. They enter my mouth and melt. They reach my diamond inside her lotus, And from her lotus come ten drops, And from the drops ten long hung letters. These transform into the Ten Wrathful Ones.

rows.english: The Golden Harvest explains these offerings as follows.  The outer offering consists of the offering of the five objects of enjoyment: the objects of the senses.  The secret offering is where we make offerings to the beings of a secret world which we are meditating upon, utilizing things that are subsumed within ourselves, such as our seed. The offering of suchness is where we go into union with a consort and experience the four levels of bliss, one by one, and thus actualize the state free of mental afflictions.

rows.english: How does the class of deep practice explain this point?  The masters Shakyamitra and Buddhaguhya both say that Prince Siddhartha went into deep meditation on the fourth concentration level, at the very limit, sitting on the banks of the Ranjana River.  All the Buddhas in every corner of the universe then snapped Their fingers; and the sound brought him up out of this meditation and urged him higher.

rows.english: As such, we would have to accept the position expressed by the master Anandagarbha.  His explanation begins by saying that our Teacher spent three countless masses of eons collecting good deeds.  Then, when he was about to reach the end of the cycle of pain, he went into deep meditation on the fourth concentration level, at the very limit, within the Heaven Below None.  At this point all the Buddhas in every corner of the universe snapped Their fingers, and the sound brought him up out of the meditation, and so on.

rows.wylie: gsang ba'i sna rtser rdzas thig bsgom pa ni, rang dang las rgya gnyis snyoms par zhugs pa las byang sems dhU tI'i mar sna gnyis 'phrad mtshams su 'pho med du 'dzin pa dang , rang dang ye rgya'i dhU tI'i mar sna gnyis 'phrad mtshams su thig le la dmigs nas bsgom pa gnyis yod do
rows.english: There are two ways in which we practice with a drop of substance at the opening of the secret channel.  For the first, we go into the meditation with a partner of the rite; when the element comes, then we hold it, without letting it move, at the juncture where the two lower openings of the channels of dance are touching.  For the second, we meditate, focusing on the drop at the juncture where the two channels of dance--those of ourselves and of our partner of the rite--are touching.

rows.english: The secret empowerment for these two refers, respectively, to the following. rows.acip: YAB YUM SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS BYANG SEMS ZHU BA SPYI BO NAS MGRIN PAR SLEB PA NA DGA' BA, MGRIN PA NAS SNYING GAR SLEB PA NA MCHOG DGA', SNYING GNAS LTE BAR SLEB PA NA KHYAD DGA', LTE BA NAS NOR BU'I RTZER SLEB PA NA LHAN SKYES KYI YE SHES SKYES PAS BDE BA DANG STONG PA NYID DBYER MED PA'I TING NGE 'DZIN LA SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS,

rows.english: The Man and Wife Sit in meditation, Which makes the Bodhi minds melt. It starts to flow down inside From the tip of Our heads; When it reaches the throat, We have Ecstasy. When it flows from the throat And reaches the heart, We have High Ecstasy. When it flows from the heart And reaches the navel, We have Incredible Ecstasy. When it flows from the navel And reaches the tip of the jewel, We have simultaneous wisdom, Which lets us sit together In meditation, our minds Fixed single-pointedly On indivisible Bliss and emptiness.

rows.acip: BAm YIG NANG GI RDO RJE BTZUN MO'I MCHOG ,CES PA'I DON PHYI'I LAS RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LA BRTEN NAS PHYAG RGYA'I BHA GA NAS RLUNG SPOS RENG GI DUD PA LTA BU BYUNG BAS NANG GI THUR SEL GYI RLUNG GYEN DU LDOG NAS LTE BA'I BTZUN MO KHAMS DMAR PO ME'I RANG BZHIN DE SBAR BA LA BRTEN NAS SPYI BO'I KHAMS DKAR PO HE RU KA'I NGO BOR GNAS PA DE ZHU, DE GNYIS SNYING KHAR 'DU 'PHROD BYAS PAS NA DE LTA BU'I RANG ZHAL MTHONG BA'I RTZE DGAS ROL BAR ZHOG CES PA DANG,
rows.wylie: baM yig nang gi rdo rje btsun mo'i mchog ,ces pa'i don phyi'i las rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pa la brten nas phyag rgya'i bha ga nas rlung spos reng gi dud pa lta bu byung bas nang gi thur sel gyi rlung gyen du ldog nas lte ba'i btsun mo khams dmar po me'i rang bzhin de sbar ba la brten nas spyi bo'i khams dkar po he ru ka'i ngo bor gnas pa de zhu, de gnyis snying khar 'du 'phrod byas pas na de lta bu'i rang zhal mthong ba'i rtse dgas rol bar zhog ces pa dang
rows.english: The next line of His prayer, which mentions "the inner Angel, Supreme Queen of Diamond, the sacred sound of vam," refers to the following process.  When you enjoy union with your outer partner of ritual, a wind comes from Her secret place, like a stream of smoke from a stick of incense.  This forces the downward-clearing wind within your own body to reverse direction and come up. This then causes the Queen at your navel (the red element, which is of the nature of fire) to blaze.  This blazing in turn causes the white element at the tip of your head (which is of the nature of Heruka) to melt down.  And then these two elements come together and collide at the heart.  What Master Tsarchen is praying for then is that He might laugh and play in the bliss of seeing the Angel's true face in this sense.

rows.acip: RAB LUS DKYIL DANG BCAS PA'AM, DE MIN RANG GCIG PU'I KHA tV'Am GA 'KHOR LO SDOM PA ZHAL PHYAG YONGS RDZOGS SAM ZHAL GCIG PHYAG GNYIS PA SKU MDOG SNGON PO RDO RJE DRIL BU 'DZIN PA PHYAG RGYA DRUG GIS BRGYAN CING, RAL PA'I THOR TSUGS KYI MDUN DU SNA TSOGS RDO RJE DANG GA-YON LA ZLA PHYED KYIS SPRAS PA THOD RLON GYI PHRENG BA'I DO SHAL CAN DU GYUR NAS RANG DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS,
rows.wylie: rab lus dkyil dang bcas pa'am, de min rang gcig pu'i kha TvAM ga 'khor lo sdom pa zhal phyag yongs rdzogs sam zhal gcig phyag gnyis pa sku mdog sngon po rdo rje dril bu 'dzin pa phyag rgya drug gis brgyan cing, ral pa'i thor tshugs kyi mdun du sna tshogs rdo rje dang ga-yon la zla phyed kyis spras pa thod rlon gyi phreng ba'i do shal can du gyur nas rang dang snyoms par zhugs
rows.english: Here it's best if the khatvanga staff held by every Angel in the secret world of the body transforms into Heruka; otherwise it can also be just the single staff which you hold.  This can either be Heruka with all His faces and arms, or else with just one face and two arms.  His holy body is blue; He holds a diamond and bell, and He wears the six accoutrement.  His yogi's dreadlocks are bound up in a topknot, and to the front of this knot is a crossed diamond.  To the knot's own left His head is adorned with a crescent moon.  He sports a garland around His neck made of fresh human skulls, and He goes into the meditation of union with us.

rows.acip: BZHI PA LA GSUM, RIG MA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS BSKYED PA'I BDUD RTZI ZOS PA'I BCUD LEN GYIS LUS KYI STOBS RGYAS PAR BYA BA, GSUNG RDO RJE'I LCES RTZA BSKUL NAS BDE BA BSKYED DE LAS BYUNG BA'I BDUD RTZI LCES MYANG BA DANG, PADMA CAN LA SOGS PA'I PHYAG RGYA RNAMS KYIS YID DGA' BAR BYA ZHING DE RNAMS KYI THUGS SUN MI DBYUNG PA MJUG SDUD DANG BCAS PA'O,,

rows.english: The fourth topic has three parts: (1) A description of how we partake of the nectar that is produced when we engage in union with our Lady of Knowledge, and how this acts as a nutritive essence which strengthens the body; (2) How we use our tongue--as the diamond of enlightened speech--to stimulate the lower end of the partner's inner channel, and produce bliss in Her; and then use our tongue again to partake of the nectar that comes from Her because of this bliss; (3) How partners such as the Lady of the Lotus are pleased, and how we must be careful never to upset their minds--along with a concluding section. * * * Choney Lama Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748) gives some additional, useful detail on the need for both inner and outer aids in his Book to Please Those with a Core of Goodness: A Brief Explanation of the Very Essence of "The Lamp that Illuminates, Totally, the Teaching on the Five Steps," on the Stage of Completion in the Teachings of the Glorious Secret Collection (ACIP digital text S00260, ff. 26b-27a):

rows.acip: DE LA 'DIR PHYI ROL GYI PHYAG RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS SROG RTZOL DU 'GRO BA'I TSUL, ZHES PA DA LTAR GYI GANG ZAG LA DNGOS SU MI DGOS PA SHAS CHE YANG, DE'I GO BA CHAGS NA BSKYED RIM SGOM BA SOGS KYI SKABS SU, YE RGYA LA BRTEN PA LA PHAN CHE BAS NYE BAR MKHO BA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: de la 'dir phyi rol gyi phyag rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pas srog rtsol du 'gro ba'i tshul, zhes pa da ltar gyi gang zag la dngos su mi dgos pa shas che yang, de'i go ba chags na bskyed rim sgom ba sogs kyi skabs su, ye rgya la brten pa la phan che bas nye bar mkho ba yin no
rows.english: We come to a point in the text then where it talks about "how we turn union with an actual, outside partner into a practice for the control of the inner winds."  Most people nowadays aren't to the point where they would actually need this, but it is useful to gain some understanding of it.  And so at junctures such as where you are practicing the stage of creation, it can be very helpful to utilize an imaginary partner--we can even say it is a necessity. * * * The points at which we practice with the two partners are identified by Je Rinpoche in His commentary to Highest Bliss (Sanvara) entitled An Illumination of Every Secret Point (ACIP digital text S05316, folio 123b).

rows.wylie: sems brtan (ye shes kyi phyag rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pa la sems brtan pa med pa rnams kyis, pa tshab chag phyi rol gyi zer, kha cig chag 'gyur gyi de mi 'thad de, rgya dpe la dgag sgra gsal bar med cing, 'grel par sems brtan pa zhes bshad pa dang 'gal bas so, ,zhes pa de ni mi 'thad de, 'grel par sems brtan pa zhes pa'i 'gyur btsas pa yin pas gnod byed du mi rung ba'i phyir dang
rows.english: When their understanding has thus become firm, they can engage in union with an outer partner.  This will bring them, the coming lines indicate, the experience of highest bliss.  (Where the text here mentions "what is done by those who do not have a firm understanding of the practice of union with an imaginary partner," we see in the translations of Patsab and Chak "an outer partner."  Some have said that Chak's translation is incorrect, since the original Sanskrit manuscript includes no clear negative grammar particle here, and because it contradicts the commentary, which at this point says "those who do have a firm understanding."  This position though is itself incorrect, since the mention of "those of firm understanding" in the commentary is using twilight language, and is thus inappropriate to use as a line to refute some other position.)

rows.acip: (DES NA 'GYUR GSAR GNYIS KA 'THUN PAR 'BYUNG BA LTAR BYA'O, ,YE RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR 'JUG PA LA SEMS BRTAN PA NI YE RGYA LA BRTEN NA, PHYI ROL GYI PHYAG RGYA LA MI LTOS PAR DE'I DGOS PA SGRUB NUS PA'I RIGS CAN GCIG YOD PAS, DES SHIN TU SPROS MED KYI SPYOD PA BYED PA YIN NO,,) PA THOB PAS PHYI ROL GYI PHYAG RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS NAS, MCHOG TU BDE BA NYAMS SU MYONG BAR BYA'O ZHES BSTAN PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR,

rows.english: (We can say then that both the newer translations work out to the same thing.  What it means to "have a firm understanding" of union with an imaginary partner is that there does exist a certain class of person who--if they practice with an imaginary partner--will be able to attain the goal of partner practice without having to rely upon an outer partner. rows.acip: 'DI LA BSKYED RIM PAS NI SPROS PA GZHAN 'DOR MOD KYANG, CHO GA'I RIM PA NI 'DRA BAR MNGON PAS, DKYIL 'KHOR RGYAL MCHOG RDZOGS PA DANG YE RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS TE, DGA' BZHI'I RIM GYIS LHAN SKYES KYI DGA' BA BSKYED DE BDE STONG SGOM MO,,
rows.wylie: 'di la bskyed rim pas ni spros pa gzhan 'dor mod kyang, cho ga'i rim pa ni 'dra bar mngon pas, dkyil 'khor rgyal mchog rdzogs pa dang ye rgya dang snyoms par zhugs te, dga' bzhi'i rim gyis lhan skyes kyi dga' ba bskyed de bde stong sgom mo
rows.english: Now it is true that in this regard a practitioner on the stage of creation gives up other kinds of elaboration; but it would seem to me that the steps of their ritual would be similar to what we've been describing.  And so they could perform the practice of the Supreme Victor of the Secret World, and engage in union with an imaginary partner, and thus bring on the four blisses.  With this then they would in stages reach the  simultaneous form of bliss, and then could meditate on bliss and voidness.

rows.acip: RDZOGS RIM GYI SKABS GSUM DU NI SGRUB THABS KYI CHO GA'I RIM PA CI RIGS PA LA BRTEN NAS YE RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA NA NANG GI RLUNG GI RNAL 'BYOR MTHAR SON PAS GROGS BYAS PA'I MTHUS, GNYIS SNANG GI SPROS PA MANG PO BCAD NAS STONG PA BZHI KHYAD PAR CAN MNGON DU BYED DO,,
rows.wylie: rdzogs rim gyi skabs gsum du ni sgrub thabs kyi cho ga'i rim pa ci rigs pa la brten nas ye rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pa na nang gi rlung gi rnal 'byor mthar son pas grogs byas pa'i mthus, gnyis snang gi spros pa mang po bcad nas stong pa bzhi khyad par can mngon du byed do
rows.english: In the three different contexts of the practice of the stage of completion then you would take some step of the ritual that involved going into union with an imaginary partner.  You thus perfect a deep practice of working with the inner winds which then lends you support in the task of eliminating a great many forms of elaboration, in the sense of perceiving things in duality.  And then you would manifest an extraordinary form of the four forms of emptiness.

rows.acip: BAm YIG NANG GI RDO RJE BTZUN MO'I MCHOG ,CES PA'I DON PHYI'I LAS RGYA DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LA BRTEN NAS PHYAG RGYA'I BHA GA NAS RLUNG SPOS RENG GI DUD PA LTA BU BYUNG BAS NANG GI THUR SEL GYI RLUNG GYEN DU LDOG NAS LTE BA'I BTZUN MO KHAMS DMAR PO ME'I RANG BZHIN DE SBAR BA LA BRTEN NAS SPYI BO'I KHAMS DKAR PO HE RU KA'I NGO BOR GNAS PA DE ZHU, DE GNYIS SNYING KHAR 'DU 'PHROD BYAS PAS NA DE LTA BU'I RANG ZHAL MTHONG BA'I RTZE DGAS ROL PAR ZHOG CES PA DANG,
rows.wylie: baM yig nang gi rdo rje btsun mo'i mchog ,ces pa'i don phyi'i las rgya dang snyoms par zhugs pa la brten nas phyag rgya'i bha ga nas rlung spos reng gi dud pa lta bu byung bas nang gi thur sel gyi rlung gyen du ldog nas lte ba'i btsun mo khams dmar po me'i rang bzhin de sbar ba la brten nas spyi bo'i khams dkar po he ru ka'i ngo bor gnas pa de zhu, de gnyis snying khar 'du 'phrod byas pas na de lta bu'i rang zhal mthong ba'i rtse dgas rol par zhog ces pa dang
rows.english: The next line of His prayer, which mentions "the inner Angel, Supreme Queen of Diamond, the sacred sound of vam," refers to the following process.  When you enjoy union with your actual, outer partner, a wind comes from Her secret place, like a stream of smoke from a stick of incense.  This forces the downward-clearing wind within your own body to reverse direction and come up. This then causes the Queen at your navel (the red element, which is of the nature of fire) to blaze.  This blazing in turn causes the white element at the tip of your head (which is of the nature of Heruka) to melt down.  And then these two elements come together and collide at the heart.  What Master Tsarchen is praying for then is that He might laugh and play in the bliss of seeing the Angel's true face in this sense.

rows.acip: SNANG BA GSAL BA DANG DE BRTAN PA RNYED NA, DE DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS NAS DGA' BZHI BSKYED PA'I LHAN SKYES KYI DUS SU, BDE STONG SBYOR NUS NA LTA BA DRAN PAR BYAS LA BDE STONG DBYER MED DU BSKYANG,
rows.wylie: snang ba gsal ba dang de brtan pa rnyed na, de dang snyoms par zhugs nas dga' bzhi bskyed pa'i lhan skyes kyi dus su, bde stong sbyor nus na lta ba dran par byas la bde stong dbyer med du bskyang
rows.english: If they keep this up over a long period of time, then they will reach a point where their visualization is very clear, and firm.  They go into union with this partner, and attain the point of the simultaneous, where they are able to bring on the four forms of bliss.  If you are able thus to achieve a union of bliss and emptiness, then try to bring to mind the correct view of reality, and maintain this vision of indivisible bliss and voidness.

rows.acip: YAB YUM SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA LAS, BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS RDO RJE NOR BU'I RTZE MOR SLEB PA NA BDE BA JI LTA BU ZHIG SKYE BA NGOS 'DZIN PA SNGA MA DAM TSIG GI PHYAG RGYA'I SKABS SU BSHAD PA BZHIN NYE BAR BRTAGS TE BDE STONG LA GOMS PA
rows.wylie: yab yum snyoms par zhugs pa las, byang chub kyi sems rdo rje nor bu'i rtse mor sleb pa na bde ba ji lta bu zhig skye ba ngos 'dzin pa snga ma dam tshig gi phyag rgya'i skabs su bshad pa bzhin nye bar brtags te bde stong la goms pa
rows.english: And then the Man and the Woman go into union.  The element of enlightenment reaches the tip of the diamond rod, and we learn to identify just which of the blisses is coming to us.  And then we undertake the same analysis that we described in the part about the partner of pledge: we accustom ourselves to the practice of bliss and voidness.

rows.acip: GONG DU BSHAD PA'I STONG GZUGS KYI PHYAG CHEN DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS MCHOG TU MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA NYAMS SU MYONG BA NI YAN LAG DRUG PA'I TING NGE 'DZIN YIN NO,,

rows.english: If we go into union with the Great Seal of the empty form, as we described it earlier, then we come to an experience of a bliss which is supremely immutable.  This then is the meditative concentration of the sixth branch of the practice.

rows.acip: MAN SNYER NYER SPYOD LNGA SPYI'I MCHOD PA DANG BSGOMS PA'I DKYIL 'KHOR LA RANG GI SA BON LA SOGS PA 'DZIN PA RNAMS KYIS MCHOD PA GSANG BA'I MCHOD PA DANG YUM DANG SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PAS DGA' BA BZHI'I RIMS KYIS NYON MONGS DAG PA'I GO 'PHANG MNGON DU BYAS PA DE KHO NA NYID KYI MCHOD PA DANG,

rows.english: The Golden Harvest explains these offerings as follows.  The outer offering consists of the offering of the five objects of enjoyment: the objects of the senses.  The secret offering is where we make offerings to the Beings of a secret world which we are meditating upon, utilizing things that are subsumed within ourselves, such as our seed. The offering of suchness is where we go into union with a partner and experience the four levels of bliss, one by one, and thus actualize the state free of mental afflictions. * * * A more traditional presentation of these four offerings appears for example in Choney Lama's Clarification of All the Major Points (ACIP digital text S00261, f. 14a):

rows.acip: MTSON BYED DPE'I (RDOR DRIL BZUNG NAS,) YUM RDO RJE (DBYINGS PHYUG MAR 'KHYUD) CING YAB YUM SNYOMS PAR ZHUGS PA'I (LHAN SKYES) KYI BDE BA DANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS STONG PA DBYER MED PA'I (BDE STONG) GI RNAM PAR (ROL BA) STE LONGS SPYOD PA'I TSUL GYI(S DGYES) BZHIN DU BZHUGS PA'O,,
rows.wylie: mtshon byed dpe'i (rdor dril bzung nas,) yum rdo rje (dbyings phyug mar 'khyud) cing yab yum snyoms par zhugs pa'i (lhan skyes) kyi bde ba dang, rang bzhin gyis stong pa dbyer med pa'i (bde stong) gi rnam par (rol ba) ste longs spyod pa'i tshul gyi(s dgyes) bzhin du bzhugs pa'o
rows.english: In His hands He holds a diamond and bell which are symbols, meant to represent something else, and He embraces--as His holy Wife--the Diamond Queen of the Empty Realm.  He is enjoying His play in the bliss and void where, when the Man and Woman go into union, They experience the pleasure of an indivisible union of simultaneous bliss and an emptiness of any inherent nature.

rows.acip: RANG BZHIN GYI GNAS 'OG MIN NI CHOS SKU LA SOGS PA RANG GI NYE LOGS KYI NAM MKHA' NAS, NAM MKHA' DVANGS PA LAS SPRIN BLO BUR DU LDANG BA LTAR PHYOGS BCU'I RGYAL BA THAMS CAD DPAL RDO RJE 'JIGS BYED KYI RTEN DANG BRTEN PA'I DKYIL 'KHOR GYI RNAM PA DPAG TU MED PAR SPYAN DRANGS NAS MA MTHA' DKYIL 'KHOR CHA TSANG BA GCIG TU GYUR BA MDUN GYI NAM MKHAR BZHUGS PAR BSAM,
rows.wylie: rang bzhin gyi gnas 'og min ni chos sku la sogs pa rang gi nye logs kyi nam mkha' nas, nam mkha' dvangs pa las sprin blo bur du ldang ba ltar phyogs bcu'i rgyal ba thams cad dpal rdo rje 'jigs byed kyi rten dang brten pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi rnam pa dpag tu med par spyan drangs nas ma mtha' dkyil 'khor cha tshang ba gcig tu gyur ba mdun gyi nam mkhar bzhugs par bsam
rows.english: These rays of light invite to you all the enlightened Victors of the entire universe, in limitless forms of the secret world of the shining Diamond Lord of Terror, and all the Holy Beings who reside in this world.  They come from the Land of Ultimate Reality, from the Dharma Body and the like, from the empty space around where you are.  They appear there like clouds suddenly forming in a crystal-clear sky.  At the very least you should try to visualize that one entire secret world of the Lord of Terror comes and appears in the air before you. 12 Mantras of the Beings of Pledge (Sadhana) The mantra

rows.acip: RNAM SMIN GYI LUS KYI PHUNG PO'I NANG NA GNAS PA NI SPRIN GYI GSEB NA GLOG 'GYU BA LTA BU'O, ,STONG PA'I NGANG NAS THOL GYIS BZHENGS PA NI SHIN TU DVANGS PA'I CHU LAS CHU BUR RDOL BA LTA BU'O, ,YAN LAG DANG NYING LAG THAMS CAD YONGS SU RDZOGS PA NI ME LONG LA RDO RJE 'CHANG GI GZUGS BRNYAN SHAR BA LTA BU'O,,
rows.wylie: rnam smin gyi lus kyi phung po'i nang na gnas pa ni sprin gyi gseb na glog 'gyu ba lta bu'o, ,stong pa'i ngang nas thol gyis bzhengs pa ni shin tu dvangs pa'i chu las chu bur rdol ba lta bu'o, ,yan lag dang nying lag thams cad yongs su rdzogs pa ni me long la rdo rje 'chang gi gzugs brnyan shar ba lta bu'o
rows.english: The way in which this body remains within the heap of the body which is a ripening of karma is like (10) the way that lightning flashes deep within a cloud.  So too the way that the body rises, all of a sudden, out of the state of emptiness is similar to how (11) a bubble pops up out of crystal-clear water.  The way in which we appear in this body with all our major and minor limbs complete in every way is similar to (12) the way the reflection of the Keeper of the Diamond would appear in a mirror.

rows.acip: NYAL LUGS PHYI MA LTAR NA, NAM MKHA' STONG PA LAS SPRIN RDOL BA'AM, CHU DVANGS PA LAS NYE'U CHUNG 'PHAR BA BZHIN DU BDE CHEN 'OD GSAL STONG PA NYID KYI NGANG LAS RANG NYID RNAL 'BYOR MA'I SKUR LAM GYIS LDANG STE, GNAS SOGS KYI BKOD PA'I KHYAD PAR PHUN SUM TSOGS PAR MOS,
rows.wylie: nyal lugs phyi ma ltar na, nam mkha' stong pa las sprin rdol ba'am, chu dvangs pa las nye'u chung 'phar ba bzhin du bde chen 'od gsal stong pa nyid kyi ngang las rang nyid rnal 'byor ma'i skur lam gyis ldang ste, gnas sogs kyi bkod pa'i khyad par phun sum tshogs par mos
rows.english: If you have been sleeping the second way, imagine that you waken all in a flash, as the Angel Herself, from a state of emptiness, from great bliss and the clear light.  Picture it like the way a cloud pops up all of a sudden in a clear blue sky, or the way a tiny fish suddenly leaps out of a pool of crystal water.  Try hard to imagine then that the place and other things around you are all perfectly excellent.

rows.acip: DES NA DANG PO NAS RMI LAM GSAL BA DANG DE MIN KYANG GNAS DBEN PA LA SOGS PA RIG PA DVANGS PA'I RGYU'I KHYAD PAR TSOGS PA'I SKABS DANG, MTSAN MO GCIG GI'ANG THO RANGS LTA BU RIG PA GSAL DUS SU, RMI LAM ZIN PAR SLA'O,,
rows.wylie: des na dang po nas rmi lam gsal ba dang de min kyang gnas dben pa la sogs pa rig pa dvangs pa'i rgyu'i khyad par tshogs pa'i skabs dang, mtshan mo gcig gi'ang tho rangs lta bu rig pa gsal dus su, rmi lam zin par sla'o
rows.english: Given all this, it is easier to maintain recognition in your dreams under the following conditions. First, when your dreams are clearer in the first place. Secondly when, even if they are not normally clear, you have created a situation with all the special conditions that lend a lucid state of mind: staying in an isolated area, and the like. And finally, even with regard to a single night, those periods--such as daybreak--when your mental state is more clear.

rows.acip: RTOGS LDAN PA'I MNAL LAM LA, RJE RIN PO CHE'I MCHOD RTEN YIN ZER BA CHA TSAD YONGS SU RDZOGS PA RTZE MO SPRIN GYI SEB LA SLEB PA, KHA DOG SHIN TU DKAR ZHING 'KHREGS PA KAR YOL GYI RTZI LTAR DVANGS PA ZHIG LA,
rows.wylie: rtogs ldan pa'i mnal lam la, rje rin po che'i mchod rten yin zer ba cha tshad yongs su rdzogs pa rtse mo sprin gyi seb la sleb pa, kha dog shin tu dkar zhing 'khregs pa kar yol gyi rtsi ltar dvangs pa zhig la
rows.english: Tokdenpa in His dream saw an offering shrine that people were saying was Je Tsongkapa's.  It was complete in all the proper dimensions, and its tip reached into the clouds. rows.english: "What kinds of beings," one may ask, "have which of the different states of birth?" All four types of birth exist with humans. An example of instant, complete birth would be humans of the very first eon. The king called "Let- Me-Nurse-You" would typify birth from warmth and moisture. A case of humans born from eggs would be the elders Drak and Nyedrak, who were offspring of a shipwrecked merchant who coupled with a female crane. Another such instance would be that of Sagala, a woman with laywoman's vows, who gave 32 eggs from which 32 boys sprang forth. Yet another case would be that of the queen of King Panchala, who gave 500 eggs. These were put into a chest that was thrown into the Ganges River. A Lichavi youth saw the chest while washing--and when he opened the lid, 500 boys sprang forth. Examples of birth from the womb would be the majority of humans of present times.

rows.english: If you make consistent efforts in this practice, you will start to dream about washing yourself; or putting on white clothes, or new clothes; seeing pus or worms or other dirty and ugly-looking things pass out of your body; or perhaps flying unaided in the sky, or things of the like.  When you have these kinds of dreams over and over, said our Lama, it is a sign that you are truly becoming cleaned of all your wrongs. Fifth: the Practice of the Lama
